---
name: slack-api
description: "Send, read, search, and manage Slack messages, channels, users, files, and reactions through the Slack Web API with a bot or user token. Use when Gemini CLI needs to post to a Slack workspace, reply in or fetch threads, list channels or members, look up users, upload files, add reactions, or run API methods such as chat.postMessage, conversations.list, conversations.history, users.list, and reactions.add."

# Slack API

## Overview

Interact with a Slack workspace over the Slack Web API (`https://slack.com/api/*`). A bundled deterministic CLI script (`scripts/slack_api.cjs`) handles authentication, request building, pagination, and response formatting, so you do not need to rewrite fetch calls for common operations.

Scope: the **Web API** only. This skill does not cover the Events API, Socket Mode, slash-command verification, or the Bolt framework.

## Authenticate First

1. Obtain an OAuth token from the user:
   - **Bot token** (`xoxb-...`) from an installed Slack app — the common choice for agent automation.
   - **User token** (`xoxp-...`) that acts as a user.
2. Export it before running the script (the script reads `SLACK_TOKEN` first, then `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`):
   ```bash
   export SLACK_TOKEN=xoxb-XXXXXXXX
   ```
3. Token scopes must cover the methods used (for example `chat:write` to post, `channels:history` to read history, `users:read` to list users). When Slack answers `missing_scope`, report the `needed` scope to the user and ask them to add it to the app and reinstall.
4. Never print, log, or embed the token in commands. Pass it via the environment only.
5. When no token is set, ask the user for one; never fabricate credentials or workspace data.

## Quick Start

Send a message to a channel:

```bash
node scripts/slack_api.cjs chat.postMessage \
  --channel C0123456789 \
  --text "Hello from an automated agent :wave:"
```

The script prints Slack's JSON response to stdout (`{"ok":true,"channel":"C...","ts":"1712345678.012345"}`) and exits 0. On failure it prints `Failure: ...` to stderr and exits 1. Run the script from the skill directory, or prefix it with the absolute skill path.

## Common Tasks

Run `node scripts/slack_api.cjs --self-test` once after installing to confirm the runtime works (offline, no token needed).

### Send a message

```bash
node scripts/slack_api.cjs chat.postMessage --channel C0123456789 --text "Body text"
```

- Use mrkdwn in `--text`: `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `` `code` ``, `:tada:`, `<https://example.com|label>`, `<@U123|Ada>`.
- Confirm with the user before posting content they did not ask to post.

### Reply inside a thread

```bash
node scripts/slack_api.cjs chat.postMessage --channel C0123456789 --thread_ts 1712345678.012345 --text "Reply text"
```

- Keep `thread_ts` as the parent message's `ts` value, passed as a string.

### Find a channel ID

```bash
node scripts/slack_api.cjs conversations.list --types public_channel,private_channel --paginate
```

- Pass IDs from the JSON output (`id` fields); do not guess IDs from channel names.

### Read conversation history

```bash
node scripts/slack_api.cjs conversations.history --channel C0123456789 --limit 50
```

- Older-to-newer: add `--oldest <epoch>`; newer-to-older: `--latest <epoch>`. Use `--paginate` to collect everything (capped at 50 pages).

### Read a thread

```bash
node scripts/slack_api.cjs conversations.replies --channel C0123456789 --ts 1712345678.012345
```

### Find users

```bash
node scripts/slack_api.cjs users.lookupByEmail --email ada@example.com
node scripts/slack_api.cjs users.list --paginate
```

### Send a DM

```bash
node scripts/slack_api.cjs conversations.open --users U0123456789
node scripts/slack_api.cjs chat.postMessage --channel D0123456789 --text "..."
```

- `conversations.open` returns the DM channel ID to use.

### Upload a file

```bash
node scripts/slack_api.cjs files.upload --channels C0123456789 --file ./report.pdf --title "Report"
```

- Requires Node.js >= 18 (`--file` uses multipart). Large uploads over ~50 MB need the `files.getUploadURLExternal` flow instead.

### Add a reaction

```bash
node scripts/slack_api.cjs reactions.add --channel C0123456789 --timestamp 1712345678.012345 --name tada
```

- The emoji name has no colons (`tada`, not `:tada:`).

### Search

```bash
node scripts/slack_api.cjs search.messages --query "quarterly report"
```

### Update or delete a message

```bash
node scripts/slack_api.cjs chat.update --channel C0123456789 --ts 1712345678.012345 --text "New text"
node scripts/slack_api.cjs chat.delete --channel C0123456789 --ts 1712345678.012345
```

## Guidelines and Pitfalls

- Treat `ts` and `thread_ts` as **strings** such as `"1712345678.012345"`. Never round them or parse them into numbers; precision loss breaks lookups.
- Fetch real IDs from `conversations.list`, `users.list`, or `users.lookupByEmail` before posting; do not invent channel/user IDs.
- A bot can only read or post where it is a member. Private channels and DMs require the token's app to have been added; expect `not_in_channel` / `channel_not_found` otherwise.
- Messages are limited to ~40,000 characters; keep agent summaries well under that and truncate long history listings with `--limit`.
- On `rate_limited`, Slack includes a `Retry-After` header; wait that many seconds before retrying, and space out calls.
- On `missing_scope`, tell the user which scope to add (the error carries the `needed` field) instead of retrying.
- Do not read or disclose private channel contents unless the user asked; respect the token's access boundaries.
- Keep the JSON response as the source of truth: check `ok`, use returned `ts`, `channel`, and IDs for follow-up calls.

## Helper Script Reference

`scripts/slack_api.cjs` is a small, dependency-free CLI:

```bash
node scripts/slack_api.cjs <api.method> [--param value ...]
```

- Any Slack method is callable as `<section>.<name>`, e.g. `chat.postMessage`, `conversations.history`.
- Parameters: `--key value` or `--key=value` (values that start with `-` need the `=` form).
- `--file PATH` attaches a local file (multipart upload). `--paginate` follows `next_cursor` and merges array results (max 50 pages).
- `--max-output N` caps printed JSON (default 20000 chars); `--raw` prints everything. Truncation notices go to stderr.
- Prints JSON to stdout; errors and notices to stderr; exit code 0 on `ok:true`, 1 otherwise. The token is never echoed.

## References

See `references/api.md` for the endpoint catalogue (parameters, typical scopes, key response fields), mrkdwn formatting reference, pagination pattern, and common error codes. Read it before choosing parameters for a method you have not used recently.

# Slack Web API Reference

Curated reference for the methods this skill most often uses. All calls go through `scripts/slack_api.cjs` as `<section>.<name>` (e.g. `chat.postMessage`) with `--param value` flags; any Web API method works even if not listed here.

## Contents
- [Tokens and scopes](#tokens-and-scopes)
- [Calling conventions](#calling-conventions)
- [Message formatting (mrkdwn)](#message-formatting-mrkdwn)
- [Messaging methods](#messaging-methods)
- [Conversation methods](#conversation-methods)
- [User methods](#user-methods)
- [Reaction methods](#reaction-methods)
- [File methods](#file-methods)
- [Search methods](#search-methods)
- [Utility methods](#utility-methods)
- [Pagination](#pagination)
- [Response envelope and common errors](#response-envelope-and-common-errors)
- [Rate limits](#rate-limits)

## Tokens and scopes

| Token | Prefix | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Bot token | `xoxb-` | From installing an app with **bot scopes**; the bot appears as its own user. Best for automation. |
| User token | `xoxp-` | Acts as the installing user with **user scopes**. |
| Legacy | `xoxa-`, `xoxs-` | Deprecated by Slack; avoid. |

Every method requires a scope. When the token lacks one, Slack returns `ok:false` with `error: "missing_scope"` and a `needed` field naming the scope; the app owner must add it and reinstall the app. Scopes below are the typical ones; consult the official method docs when in doubt.

## Calling conventions

- Base URL `https://slack.com/api/<method>`; all methods are POST.
- Send `Authorization: Bearer xoxb-...` and parameters as form-encoded fields (the helper script does this; `--file` switches to multipart).
- JSON envelope: `{"ok": true, ...}` on success, `{"ok": false, "error": "..."}` on failure.
- IDs: channel `C...`, user `U...`, DM `D...`, message timestamp `ts`. Treat every value as opaque strings.
- Timestamps are Unix epoch seconds with microseconds, e.g. `1712345678.012345`. Always pass them as strings.

## Message formatting (mrkdwn)

Slack renders lightweight markdown in `text` when `mrkdwn` is true (the default):

| You type | Renders as |
|---|---|
| `*bold*` | bold |
| `_italic_` | italic |
| `~strike~` | strikethrough |
| `` `code` `` | inline code |
| ` ``` ` + newline + text + newline + ` ``` ` | code block |
| `> quote` | blockquote |
| `:tada:` | emoji |
| `<https://example.com|Example>` | hyperlink with label |
| `<@U123456>` or `<@U123456|Ada>` | user mention |
| `<#C123456|general>` | channel link |
| `<!channel>`, `<!here>`, `<!everyone>` | special mentions (use sparingly) |

- User/channel links accept either raw IDs or ID + label.
- For rich layouts (buttons, sections, dividers), use `blocks` — a JSON array string passed via `--blocks '<json>'` — and omit `text` if `blocks` fully describe the message (Slack requires one of `text` or `blocks`).
- Formatting in `files.upload` initial comments and attachment-like fields also supports mrkdwn where documented.

## Messaging methods

Typical scope: `chat:write`.

| Method | Key params | Returns / notes |
|---|---|---|
| `chat.postMessage` | `channel`, `text` or `blocks`, `thread_ts`, `mrkdwn`, `link_names`, `reply_broadcast`, `unfurl_links`, `unfurl_media`, `username`, `icon_emoji`/`icon_url` | `channel`, `ts`, `message`. `thread_ts` posts a reply in that thread. |
| `chat.postEphemeral` | `channel`, `user`, `text` | `message_ts`; only `user` sees it. |
| `chat.update` | `channel`, `ts`, `text` or `blocks` | Edit an existing message. |
| `chat.delete` | `channel`, `ts` | Delete a message. |
| `chat.getPermalink` | `channel`, `message_ts` | `permalink` URL to a message. |
| `chat.scheduleMessage` | `channel`, `post_at` (epoch seconds), `text` | Returns `scheduled_message_id`. |

## Conversation methods

Typical scopes: `channels:read` + `groups:read` + `im:read` + `mpim:read` for reads; `channels:manage` / `groups:write` / `im:write` for management, as appropriate per type.

| Method | Key params | Returns / notes |
|---|---|---|
| `conversations.list` | `types` (`public_channel,private_channel,mpim,im`), `limit` (max 200), `cursor`, `exclude_archived` | `channels[]` with `id`, `name`, `is_*` flags. |
| `conversations.history` | `channel`, `limit` (max 200), `oldest`, `latest`, `inclusive`, `cursor` | `messages[]` (newest first), `has_more`, `response_metadata.next_cursor`. |
| `conversations.replies` | `channel`, `ts` | All messages in the thread whose parent is `ts`. |
| `conversations.info` | `channel`, `include_num_members` | The conversation object. |
| `conversations.members` | `channel`, `limit`, `cursor` | `members[]` (user IDs). |
| `conversations.open` | `users` (comma-separated IDs) or `channel` | DM/channel `channel.id`; use before posting DMs. |
| `conversations.join` / `leave` | `channel` | Public channel membership (bot). |
| `conversations.create` | `name`, `is_private` | New channel; returns the conversation. |
| `conversations.invite` / `kick` | `channel`, `users` | Manage membership. |
| `conversations.archive` / `unarchive` | `channel` | Archive state. |
| `conversations.rename` | `channel`, `name` | Rename. |
| `conversations.mark` | `channel`, `ts` | Move the read cursor. |

Notes:
- Private channels, DMs, and multi-party DMs behave like channels for these methods; the token's app must have access.
- `conversations.history`/`replies` also need `channels:history` (public), `groups:history` (private), `im:history` (DM), or `mpim:history`.

## User methods

Typical scopes: `users:read`; email lookup needs `users:read.email`.

| Method | Key params | Returns / notes |
|---|---|---|
| `users.list` | `limit` (max 200), `cursor` | `members[]` with `id`, `name`, `real_name`, `profile.email`, `deleted`. |
| `users.info` | `user` | The user object. |
| `users.lookupByEmail` | `email` | `user` object; 404-style `users_not_found` when absent. |
| `users.getPresence` | `user` | `presence` (`active`, `away`). |
| `users.conversations` | `limit`, `cursor`, `types` | Conversations the user can access. |

## Reaction methods

Typical scopes: `reactions:read`, `reactions:write`.

| Method | Key params | Returns / notes |
|---|---|---|
| `reactions.add` | `channel`, `name`, `timestamp` | Emoji name **without** colons. |
| `reactions.remove` | `channel`, `name`, `timestamp` | Remove the caller's reaction. |
| `reactions.get` | `channel`, `timestamp` | `message.reactions[]` with counts and user lists. |

## File methods

Typical scopes: `files:read`, `files:write`.

| Method | Key params | Returns / notes |
|---|---|---|
| `files.upload` | `file` (via `--file`), `channels`, `filename`, `title`, `initial_comment`, `content`, `thread_ts` | `file` object with `id`, `permalink`, `url_private`. Requires the bot to be in the target channel. |
| `files.info` | `file` | Metadata; fetch content via `url_private` with the token as a Bearer header. |
| `files.list` | `limit`, `cursor`, `channel`, `user` | `files[]`. |
| `files.delete` | `file` | Deletes a file. |

Notes:
- `--file PATH` sends a real multipart upload; `--content "text"` uploads a text-only snippet without a file.
- Files over roughly 50 MB need the two-step flow: `files.getUploadURLExternal` then `files.completeUploadExternal` (out of scope for the helper's single call).

## Search methods

Typical scope: `search:read`.

| Method | Key params | Returns / notes |
|---|---|---|
| `search.messages` | `query`, `count`, `sort` (`score`/`timestamp`), `sort_dir`, `page` | `messages.matches[]`; each match includes `channel`, `ts`, `text`, `permalink`. |
| `search.files` | `query`, `count`, `page` | `files.matches[]`. |

Search is workspace-wide and respects the token's access; it can be slow to index new content.

## Utility methods

| Method | Notes |
|---|---|
| `auth.test` | Verify the token; returns `team`, `user`, `url`, `team_id`, `user_id`. No scope needed. |
| `api.test` | Connectivity check; returns `ok:true`. |

## Pagination

Cursor-based. Each page returns `response_metadata.next_cursor` when more data exists (older methods may use `next_cursor` at top level).

- One page: `node scripts/slack_api.cjs conversations.history --channel C123 --limit 200`
- Manual next page: re-run with `--cursor <next_cursor>`.
- Collect everything: add `--paginate`; the helper follows cursors (up to 50 pages) and merges array fields (`messages`, `channels`, `members`, ...) into one response. `has_more` is set to false in merged output. Merged output can be large — raise `--max-output` or use `--raw` if needed.
- Prefer `--paginate` over repeated manual calls for listing tasks; for huge workspaces, filter early (`types`, `query`, `oldest`/`latest`, `limit`).

## Response envelope and common errors

Success looks like `{"ok": true, ...}`. Common `error` values:

| Error | Meaning / action |
|---|---|
| `not_authed`, `invalid_auth` | Token missing or malformed; check the env var. |
| `account_inactive`, `token_revoked` | Token was disabled or revoked; ask the user for a new one. |
| `missing_scope` | Add the scope in the `needed` field to the app and reinstall. |
| `rate_limited` | HTTP 429 with `Retry-After` header; wait and retry. |
| `channel_not_found` | Wrong ID, or the bot lacks access to that channel. |
| `not_in_channel` | Bot must be added/invited first. |
| `is_archived` | Unarchive the channel before posting. |
| `user_not_found` | Wrong user ID. |

# Slack Web API Reference

Curated reference for the methods this skill most often uses. All calls go through `scripts/slack_api.cjs` as `<section>.<name>` (e.g. `chat.postMessage`) with `--param value` flags; any Web API method works even if not listed here.

## Contents
- [Tokens and scopes](#tokens-and-scopes)
- [Calling conventions](#calling-conventions)
- [Message formatting (mrkdwn)](#message-formatting-mrkdwn)
- [Messaging methods](#messaging-methods)
- [Conversation methods](#conversation-methods)
- [User methods](#user-methods)
- [Reaction methods](#reaction-methods)
- [File methods](#file-methods)
- [Search methods](#search-methods)
- [Utility methods](#utility-methods)
- [Pagination](#pagination)
- [Response envelope and common errors](#response-envelope-and-common-errors)
- [Rate limits](#rate-limits)

## Tokens and scopes

| Token | Prefix | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Bot token | `xoxb-` | From installing an app with **bot scopes**; the bot appears as its own user. Best for automation. |
| User token | `xoxp-` | Acts as the installing user with **user scopes**. |
| Legacy | `xoxa-`, `xoxs-` | Deprecated by Slack; avoid. |

Every method requires a scope. When the token lacks one, Slack returns `ok:false` with `error: "missing_scope"` and a `needed` field naming the scope; the app owner must add it and reinstall the app. Scopes below are the typical ones; consult the official method docs when in doubt.

## Calling conventions

- Base URL `https://slack.com/api/<method>`; all methods are POST.
- Send `Authorization: Bearer xoxb-...` and parameters as form-encoded fields (the helper script does this; `--file` switches to multipart).
- JSON envelope: `{"ok": true, ...}` on success, `{"ok": false, "error": "..."}` on failure.
- IDs: channel `C...`, user `U...`, DM `D...`, message timestamp `ts`. Treat every value as opaque strings.
- Timestamps are Unix epoch seconds with microseconds, e.g. `1712345678.012345`. Always pass them as strings.

## Message formatting (mrkdwn)

Slack renders lightweight markdown in `text` when `mrkdwn` is true (the default):

| You type | Renders as |
|---|---|
| `*bold*` | bold |
| `_italic_` | italic |
| `~strike~` | strikethrough |
| `` `code` `` | inline code |
| ` ``` ` + newline + text + newline + ` ``` ` | code block |
| `> quote` | blockquote |
| `:tada:` | emoji |
| `<https://example.com|Example>` | hyperlink with label |
| `<@U123456>` or `<@U123456|Ada>` | user mention |
| `<#C123456|general>` | channel link |
| `<!channel>`, `<!here>`, `<!everyone>` | special mentions (use sparingly) |

- User/channel links accept either raw IDs or ID + label.
- For rich layouts (buttons, sections, dividers), use `blocks` — a JSON array string passed via `--blocks '<json>'` — and omit `text` if `blocks` fully describe the message (Slack requires one of `text` or `blocks`).
- Formatting in `files.upload` initial comments and attachment-like fields also supports mrkdwn where documented.

## Messaging methods

Typical scope: `chat:write`.

| Method | Key params | Returns / notes |
|---|---|---|
| `chat.postMessage` | `channel`, `text` or `blocks`, `thread_ts`, `mrkdwn`, `link_names`, `reply_broadcast`, `unfurl_links`, `unfurl_media`, `username`, `icon_emoji`/`icon_url` | `channel`, `ts`, `message`. `thread_ts` posts a reply in that thread. |
| `chat.postEphemeral` | `channel`, `user`, `text` | `message_ts`; only `user` sees it. |
| `chat.update` | `channel`, `ts`, `text` or `blocks` | Edit an existing message. |
| `chat.delete` | `channel`, `ts` | Delete a message. |
| `chat.getPermalink` | `channel`, `message_ts` | `permalink` URL to a message. |
| `chat.scheduleMessage` | `channel`, `post_at` (epoch seconds), `text` | Returns `scheduled_message_id`. |

## Conversation methods

Typical scopes: `channels:read` + `groups:read` + `im:read` + `mpim:read` for reads; `channels:manage` / `groups:write` / `im:write` for management, as appropriate per type.

| Method | Key params | Returns / notes |
|---|---|---|
| `conversations.list` | `types` (`public_channel,private_channel,mpim,im`), `limit` (max 200), `cursor`, `exclude_archived` | `channels[]` with `id`, `name`, `is_*` flags. |
| `conversations.history` | `channel`, `limit` (max 200), `oldest`, `latest`, `inclusive`, `cursor` | `messages[]` (newest first), `has_more`, `response_metadata.next_cursor`. |
| `conversations.replies` | `channel`, `ts` | All messages in the thread whose parent is `ts`. |
| `conversations.info` | `channel`, `include_num_members` | The conversation object. |
| `conversations.members` | `channel`, `limit`, `cursor` | `members[]` (user IDs). |
| `conversations.open` | `users` (comma-separated IDs) or `channel` | DM/channel `channel.id`; use before posting DMs. |
| `conversations.join` / `leave` | `channel` | Public channel membership (bot). |
| `conversations.create` | `name`, `is_private` | New channel; returns the conversation. |
| `conversations.invite` / `kick` | `channel`, `users` | Manage membership. |
| `conversations.archive` / `unarchive` | `channel` | Archive state. |
| `conversations.rename` | `channel`, `name` | Rename. |
| `conversations.mark` | `channel`, `ts` | Move the read cursor. |

Notes:
- Private channels, DMs, and multi-party DMs behave like channels for these methods; the token's app must have access.
- `conversations.history`/`replies` also need `channels:history` (public), `groups:history` (private), `im:history` (DM), or `mpim:history`.

## User methods

Typical scopes: `users:read`; email lookup needs `users:read.email`.

| Method | Key params | Returns / notes |
|---|---|---|
| `users.list` | `limit` (max 200), `cursor` | `members[]` with `id`, `name`, `real_name`, `profile.email`, `deleted`. |
| `users.info` | `user` | The user object. |
| `users.lookupByEmail` | `email` | `user` object; 404-style `users_not_found` when absent. |
| `users.getPresence` | `user` | `presence` (`active`, `away`). |
| `users.conversations` | `limit`, `cursor`, `types` | Conversations the user can access. |

## Reaction methods

Typical scopes: `reactions:read`, `reactions:write`.

| Method | Key params | Returns / notes |
|---|---|---|
| `reactions.add` | `channel`, `name`, `timestamp` | Emoji name **without** colons. |
| `reactions.remove` | `channel`, `name`, `timestamp` | Remove the caller's reaction. |
| `reactions.get` | `channel`, `timestamp` | `message.reactions[]` with counts and user lists. |

## File methods

Typical scopes: `files:read`, `files:write`.

| Method | Key params | Returns / notes |
|---|---|---|
| `files.upload` | `file` (via `--file`), `channels`, `filename`, `title`, `initial_comment`, `content`, `thread_ts` | `file` object with `id`, `permalink`, `url_private`. Requires the bot to be in the target channel. |
| `files.info` | `file` | Metadata; fetch content via `url_private` with the token as a Bearer header. |
| `files.list` | `limit`, `cursor`, `channel`, `user` | `files[]`. |
| `files.delete` | `file` | Deletes a file. |

Notes:
- `--file PATH` sends a real multipart upload; `--content "text"` uploads a text-only snippet without a file.
- Files over roughly 50 MB need the two-step flow: `files.getUploadURLExternal` then `files.completeUploadExternal` (out of scope for the helper's single call).

## Search methods

Typical scope: `search:read`.

| Method | Key params | Returns / notes |
|---|---|---|
| `search.messages` | `query`, `count`, `sort` (`score`/`timestamp`), `sort_dir`, `page` | `messages.matches[]`; each match includes `channel`, `ts`, `text`, `permalink`. |
| `search.files` | `query`, `count`, `page` | `files.matches[]`. |

Search is workspace-wide and respects the token's access; it can be slow to index new content.

## Utility methods

| Method | Notes |
|---|---|
| `auth.test` | Verify the token; returns `team`, `user`, `url`, `team_id`, `user_id`. No scope needed. |
| `api.test` | Connectivity check; returns `ok:true`. |

## Pagination

Cursor-based. Each page returns `response_metadata.next_cursor` when more data exists (older methods may use `next_cursor` at top level).

- One page: `node scripts/slack_api.cjs conversations.history --channel C123 --limit 200`
- Manual next page: re-run with `--cursor <next_cursor>`.
- Collect everything: add `--paginate`; the helper follows cursors (up to 50 pages) and merges array fields (`messages`, `channels`, `members`, ...) into one response. `has_more` is set to false in merged output. Merged output can be large — raise `--max-output` or use `--raw` if needed.
- Prefer `--paginate` over repeated manual calls for listing tasks; for huge workspaces, filter early (`types`, `query`, `oldest`/`latest`, `limit`).

## Response envelope and common errors

Success looks like `{"ok": true, ...}`. Common `error` values:

| Error | Meaning / action |
|---|---|
| `not_authed`, `invalid_auth` | Token missing or malformed; check the env var. |
| `account_inactive`, `token_revoked` | Token was disabled or revoked; ask the user for a new one. |
| `missing_scope` | Add the scope in the `needed` field to the app and reinstall. |
| `rate_limited` | HTTP 429 with `Retry-After` header; wait and retry. |
| `channel_not_found` | Wrong ID, or the bot lacks access to that channel. |
| `not_in_channel` | Bot must be added/invited first. |
| `is_archived` | Unarchive the channel before posting. |
| `user_not_found` | Wrong user ID. |
| `invalid_ts_latest` / `invalid_ts_oldest` / `ts_invalid` | Timestamp malformed or not a string; pass full epoch with microseconds. |
| `msg_too_long` | Text exceeds the ~40,000 character limit; trim or split. |
| `invalid_blocks` | `blocks` JSON failed validation. |
| `restricted_action` | Enterprise/org policy blocked the action. |
| `internal_error` | Transient Slack-side failure; retry once. |

## Rate limits

Slack assigns each method a tier (Tier 1 most permissive through Tier 4 most restrictive) instead of a flat global limit. Practical rules:

- Space calls out; do not hammer pagination or search.
- When you get `rate_limited` with `Retry-After: <seconds>`, wait exactly that long before the next request.
- Batch-friendly patterns (send, list, search) tolerate pauses between calls; long listing runs should pause ~1 second per page unless a `Retry-After` says otherwise.

3. Token scopes must cover the methods used (for example `chat:write` to post, `channels:history` to read history, `users:read` to list users). When Slack answers `missing_scope`, report the `needed` scope to the user and ask them to add it to the app and reinstall.
4. Never print, log, or embed the token in commands. Pass it via the environment only.
5. When no token is set, ask the user for one; never fabricate credentials or workspace data.

## Quick Start

Send a message to a channel:

```bash
node scripts/slack_api.cjs chat.postMessage \
  --channel C0123456789 \
  --text "Hello from an automated agent :wave:"
```

The script prints Slack's JSON response to stdout (`{"ok":true,"channel":"C...","ts":"1712345678.012345"}`) and exits 0. On failure it prints `Failure: ...` to stderr and exits 1. Run the script from the skill directory, or prefix it with the absolute skill path.

## Common Tasks

Run `node scripts/slack_api.cjs --self-test` once after installing to confirm the runtime works (offline, no token needed).

### Send a message

```bash
node scripts/slack_api.cjs chat.postMessage --channel C0123456789 --text "Body text"
```

- Use mrkdwn in `--text`: `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `` `code` ``, `:tada:`, `<https://example.com|label>`, `<@U123|Ada>`.
- Confirm with the user before posting content they did not ask to post.

### Reply inside a thread

```bash
node scripts/slack_api.cjs chat.postMessage --channel C0123456789 --thread_ts 1712345678.012345 --text "Reply text"
```

- Keep `thread_ts` as the parent message's `ts` value, passed as a string.

### Find a channel ID

```bash
node scripts/slack_api.cjs conversations.list --types public_channel,private_channel --paginate
```

- Pass IDs from the JSON output (`id` fields); do not guess IDs from channel names.

### Read conversation history

```bash
node scripts/slack_api.cjs conversations.history --channel C0123456789 --limit 50
```

- Older-to-newer: add `--oldest <epoch>`; newer-to-older: `--latest <epoch>`. Use `--paginate` to collect everything (capped at 50 pages).

### Read a thread

```bash
node scripts/slack_api.cjs conversations.replies --channel C0123456789 --ts 1712345678.012345
```

### Find users

```bash
node scripts/slack_api.cjs users.lookupByEmail --email ada@example.com
node scripts/slack_api.cjs users.list --paginate
```

### Send a DM

```bash
node scripts/slack_api.cjs conversations.open --users U0123456789
node scripts/slack_api.cjs chat.postMessage --channel D0123456789 --text "..."
```

- `conversations.open` returns the DM channel ID to use.

### Upload a file

```bash
node scripts/slack_api.cjs files.upload --channels C0123456789 --file ./report.pdf --title "Report"
```

- Requires Node.js >= 18 (`--file` uses multipart). Large uploads over ~50 MB need the `files.getUploadURLExternal` flow instead.

### Add a reaction

```bash
node scripts/slack_api.cjs reactions.add --channel C0123456789 --timestamp 1712345678.012345 --name tada
```

- The emoji name has no colons (`tada`, not `:tada:`).

```bash

## Guidelines and Pitfalls

- Treat `ts` and `thread_ts` as **strings** such as `"1712345678.012345"`. Never round them or parse them into numbers; precision loss breaks lookups.
- Fetch real IDs from `conversations.list`, `users.list`, or `users.lookupByEmail` before posting; do not invent channel/user IDs.
- A bot can only read or post where it is a member. Private channels and DMs require the token's app to have been added; expect `not_in_channel` / `channel_not_found` otherwise.
- Messages are limited to ~40,000 characters; keep agent summaries well under that and truncate long history listings with `--limit`.
- On `rate_limited`, Slack includes a `Retry-After` header; wait that many seconds before retrying, and space out calls.
- On `missing_scope`, tell the user which scope to add (the error carries the `needed` field) instead of retrying.
- Do not read or disclose private channel contents unless the user asked; respect the token's access boundaries.
- Keep the JSON response as the source of truth: check `ok`, use returned `ts`, `channel`, and IDs for follow-up calls.

## Helper Script Reference

`scripts/slack_api.cjs` is a small, dependency-free CLI:

```bash
node scripts/slack_api.cjs <api.method> [--param value ...]
```

- Any Slack method is callable as `<section>.<name>`, e.g. `chat.postMessage`, `conversations.history`.
- Parameters: `--key value` or `--key=value` (values that start with `-` need the `=` form).
- `--file PATH` attaches a local file (multipart upload). `--paginate` follows `next_cursor` and merges array results (max 50 pages).
- `--max-output N` caps printed JSON (default 20000 chars); `--raw` prints everything. Truncation notices go to stderr.
- Prints JSON to stdout; errors and notices to stderr; exit code 0 on `ok:true`, 1 otherwise. The token is never echoed.
